label: a6-059-fs-separable-spaces-are-second-countable
tail:
### FINDINGS

No fatal defects found. The proof correctly refutes the statement by exhibiting the lower-limit topology on ℝ as a separable but not second‑countable space. The reasoning is logically sound, and all cited dependencies supply exactly what is claimed.

**Checks performed:**
- **Step 1.1 (separability):** ℚ is at most countable (thm‑rationals‑countable). For any basic open set \([a,b)\) with \(a<b\), lem‑rat‑embeds‑dense provides a rational \(q\) with \(a<q<b\), so \(q\in[a,b)\). Hence ℚ meets every nonempty basic open set, so it is dense (def‑separable‑space). The gap between “meets every basic open set” and “meets every open set” is standard and instantly closed by the fact that the topology is generated by the basis.
- **Step 1.2 (non‑second‑countable):** Assuming an at most countable basis ℬ, it is nonempty (as ℝ≠∅ and a basis must cover ℝ). By lem‑countable‑iff‑surjection‑from‑n there exists a surjection ℕ→ℬ, giving an enumeration \((B_n)\). For any \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), \([x,x+1)\) is open in the lower‑limit topology, so by the basis property (thm‑basis‑criterion) there exists \(B\in\mathcal{B}\) with \(x\in B\subseteq[x,x+1)\); the corresponding index belongs to \(E_x\), so \(E_x\neq\varnothing\). Define \(n(x)=\min E_x\). If \(x<y\) and \(n(x)=n(y)=n\), then \(x\in B_n\subseteq[x,x+1)\) and \(B_n\subseteq[y,y+1)\), forcing \(x\in[y,y+1)\Rightarrow y\le x\), contradiction. Thus \(x\mapsto n(x)\) is an injection \(\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{N}\). This contradicts the uncountability of ℝ (thm‑r‑uncountable: ℝ is neither finite nor countably infinite, and an injection into ℕ would make it so). The argument uses no choice: the enumeration is given by the lemma’s surjection (which the lemma obtains without choice), and the least‑index selection uses the well‑ordering of ℕ.
- **Citations:** [L1] accurately summarises thm‑rationals‑countable, lem‑rat‑embeds‑dense, and thm‑r‑uncountable. [L2] matches the characterisation in thm‑basis‑criterion. [L3] matches the definitions. [L4] matches lem‑countable‑iff‑surjection‑from‑n.
- **Title and Statement:** The item correctly presents and refutes the claim “Every separable space is second countable”.

0 fatal, 0 nonfatal
